entries.test: Public evaluations showing reliable agents operating without one or more of the listed capabilities would refute the claimed necessary prerequisites.
entries.note: In context, “agents” means reliably functioning agents, rather than merely systems marketed as agents.

entries.test: Public evaluations and technical descriptions of generative-AI-only agents would show whether recurring failures in the listed capabilities prevent reliable performance.
entries.note: The normalization reasonably repairs the sentence’s apparent typos and resolves its reference to the preceding capabilities.

entries.test: Repeated public trials of AI agents would show whether prompts produce both successful and anomalous outcomes whose occurrence is difficult to predict in advance.
entries.note: This is a firm forecast of variable performance, not merely a statement that failures are possible; no deadline is specified.
